principle: The reviewer froze v1 BEFORE execution and it produced 5 literal REDs. Those 5 REDs are PRESERVED in observations/after/oc7_adversarial_v1.{xml,log} and are NOT deleted or suppressed. Each was adjudicated individually. All 5 were found to be REVIEWER EXPECTATION ERRORS about the module's declared contract, not OC6 defects. Only those 5 expectations were changed. No OC5E/OC6/original test source was edited, xfailed or skipped at any point.

corrections.reviewer_expected: 'note\u2460' is an alias of allowed field 'note' and is refused as a duplicate
corrections.reasoning: U+2460 CIRCLED DIGIT ONE is NFKC-compatible with the ASCII digit '1'. It is therefore NOT a normalization-equivalent spelling of 'note' but of the distinct name 'note1'. The module's fail-closed refusal of the derived name 'note1' is correct behaviour. My alias list wrongly included it.
corrections.change: removed the enclosed_alphanumeric case from the alias parametrization

corrections.reviewer_expected: a lone fullwidth alias is reported as unapproved_field
corrections.reasoning: _normalized(fullwidth 'request_id') == 'request_id', which IS an allowed top-level key. The A1 contract constrains the NORMALIZED key, never the raw spelling, so a lone fullwidth spelling is a legitimate instance of that allowed field and is not a duplicate (no collision exists). The module is correct.
corrections.change: replaced with test_A1_lone_alias_of_allowed_field_is_admitted_as_that_allowed_field (asserts equivalence with the canonical spelling) plus test_A1_alias_that_normalizes_to_a_DIFFERENT_name_is_unapproved

corrections.reviewer_expected: a deeply nested packet raises excess_nesting
corrections.actual_module_behaviour: my constructed packet was only 2 levels deep because the loop reassigned the same dict
corrections.reasoning: My builder never increased depth, so I asserted against a valid shallow packet that correctly returned []. The excess_nesting guard was never actually exercised.
corrections.change: added a correct _nest(depth) builder; test_G8_excessive_nesting_is_refused (depth 12 must raise excess_nesting) and test_G8_reasonable_nesting_is_admitted (depth 2 must not)

corrections.reviewer_expected: mutating a committed capsule is refused
corrections.reasoning: CustodyCapsule is a frozen dataclass, so plain assignment never reached the seal comparison I intended to probe. A hostile in-process tamper must bypass the freeze.
corrections.change: used object.__setattr__ to model the real hostile mutation, which then correctly raised EditAfterFreezeError

corrections.actual_module_behaviour: False; CONFLICT_PAIRS declares SEMANTIC_ADJUDICATOR x SCENARIO_AUTHOR but not CUSTODIAN x SEMANTIC_ADJUDICATOR
corrections.reasoning: I asserted a pair the module never declared. The effective contract IS the CONFLICT_PAIRS frozenset itself, which require_second_signature relies on. Declaring an undeclared conflict would have been my own unsanctioned policy change.
corrections.change: replaced with test_G10_role_conflict_matrix_matches_the_declared_pairs plus test_G10_conflict_matrix_is_symmetric (permutation sweep over all Role pairs)
